title: Nonstandard IdP behaviors and attribute mapping guidance for SSO/SAML
creator: Aditi Sharma
description: Document covering uncommon IdP behaviors (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping) and recommended attribute mappings and mitigation patterns for RBAC v2 + audit logging. Focused on edge cases that cause silent failures or incorrect role bindings in production.
background: Our RBAC v2 rollout depends on reliable SAML attribute delivery for role and group bindings. Several customers reported permission drift after SSO configuration changes. Investigation traced root causes to IdP-specific quirks (NameID formats, group claim truncation, unsigned assertions when configured, RelayState handling).

This ticket captures compatibility guidance, concrete mapping patterns, and a prioritised troubleshooting checklist for on-call engineers and SREs. It also defines minimum audit events to detect mapping regressions.
Targets: minimize manual remediations, provide deterministic mappings for role assignment, and ensure audit trails show attribute deltas and assertion metadata.
Scope excludes SAML SP-initiated logout and deep IdP provisioning APIs; those will be separate tickets.
Reviewed against customer incidents: INC-23412, INC-23901, and regression tests in staging-ssorun-3.
decisions: Canonical attribute for RBAC v2 role assignment will be 'redwood_roles' (comma-separated) with fallback to 'groups' and 'memberOf' if absent.
We will accept NameID in formats: emailAddress and persistent; if NameID not present, use 'email' claim. Configuration will surface a warning when NameID/email mismatch occurs.
Default clock skew tolerance: 180 seconds for assertion not-before/expiry checks (aligns with common IdP defaults).
Audit logs must include raw SAML assertion fingerprint (SHA256), parsed attribute hash, subject identifier, IdP entityID, and timestamp for every successful and failed login.
For Azure AD, treat group claims sent as nested JSON or in over-the-limit continuation mechanism as 'partial' and require group-sync via SCIM or manual mapping for large orgs.

We will surface a best-effort compatibility note for unsigned assertions: allow only for dedicated test tenants when 'allow_unsigned_assertions' feature flag is enabled and machine-to-machine approval is recorded.
Adopt a defensive mapping precedence: redwood_roles > explicit role mapping table (admin mapping) > groups > email-derived default role (viewer).
Default behavior on missing role attributes: assign minimal 'viewer' role and open an audit alert for the tenant admin to review.
Reject assertion encryption as unsupported for initial ship; document migration steps for customers who require encrypted assertions (future ticket).
tradeoffs: Allowing unsigned assertions (flagged) increases friction for strict security-conscious customers; mitigated by restricting to non-production tenants and logging the risk in audit.
Lenient fallback (email->role) reduces login failures but can silently over-provision if IdP config changed; mitigated by audit alerts and defaulting to 'viewer'.
Adding group continuation support for Azure (handling >150 groups) increases engineering complexity; initial release prefers recommending SCIM or custom role mappings.
Tighter clock skew (e.g., 60s) would be more secure but increases false rejects for heterogeneous IdP clocks; we chose 180s to reduce customer support overhead.
Deferring assertion encryption support shortens delivery time but requires a clear opt-in path for regulated customers.
implementation_plan: 1) Add new attribute parser that extracts: NameID, email, redwood_roles, groups, memberOf, role_hint. Normalize to lowercase and trim whitespace.
2) Implement mapping precedence logic in auth pipeline: redwood_roles -> static role table -> groups -> email default.

3) Add telemetry hooks: emit 'saml.assertion.received', 'saml.mapping.applied', 'saml.session.created', 'saml.mapping.missing' with standardized fields (subject, idp_entity, assertion_sha256, mapping_source).
4) Create IdP compatibility notes surface in Console setup flow with automated checks for common misconfigurations (ACS mismatch, NameID missing, group truncation warning).
5) Roll out feature-flagged 'allow_unsigned_assertions' restricted to enterprise test tenants; require acceptance in admin console and email verification.
6) Add automated test scenarios to staging: Okta default, Okta with groups-as-claims, Azure with groups over-limit, Google Workspace with custom attribute mapping, Ping with NameID persistent.
7) Ship docs and run training for solutions engineers; include a short runbook for on-call.
testing_matrix: Scenario A - Okta: NameID=email, groups via 'groups' claim, role mapping via 'redwood_roles' -> expected: direct role assignment from 'redwood_roles'
Scenario B - Okta: groups sent as URIs and pagination -> expected: groups incomplete -> alert 'group.continuation.required' and fallback to role table
Scenario C - Azure AD: group-overflow with 'hasMoreGroups' -> expected: do not assume full membership; require SCIM or mapping; UI should show 'partial groups' badge
Scenario D - Google Workspace: custom attribute 'roles' as multi-valued SAML attribute -> parser should join values and map to roles
Scenario E - Ping: NameID persistent with differing email claim -> detect mismatch and create admin notification; default to NameID for subject,
Scenario F - Edge: Missing NameID and no email attribute -> reject login and log 'saml.subject.missing' with actionable message to admin
troubleshooting_playbook: Step 1: Reproduce using a test tenant and SAML tracer (https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/saml-tracer/ or https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/saml-tracer-equivalent). Capture assertion, check NameID and attributes.
Step 2: Compute SHA256 of raw assertion and compare to audit logs: echo -n '<assertion>' | sha256sum. Look up in logging UI for 'saml.assertion.received'.
Step 3: Verify ACS/EntityID: common cause of redirect loop/401 is ACS mismatch. Confirm RelayState is forwarded by SP and not stripped by intermediary proxy.
Step 4: If groups appear truncated: check IdP 'groups' claim config; for Azure see docs on group claims and overage; recommend SCIM where >150 groups are expected.
Step 5: For name/email mismatches: advise tenant admin to set 'Primary email' claim or set NameID Format to 'emailAddress'. Provide remediation link to onboarding doc.
Step 6: When 'allow_unsigned_assertions' is not set and assertion is unsigned, instruct admin to enable assertion signing in IdP and check signing certificate validity.
Step 7: If persistent login failures after mapping changes, trigger 'saml.mapping.missing' alert and provide a one-click rollback to previous mapping in Console.

Common commands and links: GitHub staging runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth/pull/812, Confluence doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SEC/pages/SSO+IdP+Guidance, Incident postmortem: drive.google.com/drive/folders/incident-23412.
audit_logging_requirements: Every SSO attempt MUST emit: event_type, tenant_id, subject_id (NameID or email), idp_entity_id, assertion_sha256, mapping_source (redwood_roles/groups/email), outcome (success/failure), failure_reason (if any), timestamp, request_id.
On mapping changes (admin updates Role Mapping table), log: event_type='mapping.update', actor, before_hash, after_hash, change_diff, approved_by (if applicable).
When fallback role is applied (viewer), emit 'mapping.fallback' with evidence: missing_attributes list and original_assertion_snippet (base64).
Retention: identity-critical events (login success/fail, mapping.update, mapping.fallback) must be retained for 13 months for compliance review; lower-volume debug logs may be rotated earlier.
Expose audit queries in Console: filters for idp_entity_id, subject_id, assertion_sha256, event_type, and time range.
Alerting: create a tenant-level alert when >5% of daily logins use fallback mapping or when assertion parsing fails for >1% of attempts.
rbac_mapping_examples: Recommended canonical mapping pattern (SAML attribute -> Redwood):
SAML 'redwood_roles' -> Redwood 'roles' (string list, comma-separated): e.g., 'admin,infra-operator', parsed to ['admin','infra-operator']
SAML 'groups' -> group membership mapping table -> role bindings (prefix mapping allowed, e.g., 'eng-*' -> 'engineer').
SAML 'memberOf' (LDAP DN) -> extract CN or uid and map via normalize_name function.
Example assertion line we will log (sample):
saml.assertion.received: tenant=acme, subject=jane.doe@acme.com, idp=okta://acme.okta.com, assertion_sha256=3b1f2..., mapping_source=redwood_roles, mapped_roles=[admin], outcome=success
If only email present, default mapping behavior: assign 'viewer' and log 'mapping.fallback'.
For admin grant via SAML attribute 'is_admin'='true', require admin confirmation on first use (two-step): Admin must acknowledge elevated role in Console; record 'admin.first_confirm' event.

acceptance_criteria: Automated parser normalizes attributes and passes unit tests for all listed IdP scenarios.
Mapping precedence logic applied consistently and covered by integration tests in staging.
Console displays compatibility warnings for at least 3 common misconfigs (ACS mismatch, missing NameID, group truncation).
Audit events emitted with required fields and discoverable in Console within 60 seconds of login.
Documentation published and solutions-engineers trained; at least two customer test tenants onboarded without manual mapping fixes.
notes: Follow-up tickets: encrypted assertions support (ENG-70700), SCIM group sync enhancements (ENG-70600), SLO logout handling (ENG-70999).
Consider adding 'attribute-validator' step that enforces presence of required attributes for high-privilege roles.
Communicate to onboarding: avoid using NameID formats that omit email for orgs where email is primary identity.
Keep developer-facing error messages informative but not verbose about internals (avoid leaking assertion contents in public logs).
